content:
rachel: Quick pulse — ran a targeted sanity pass for ceres-13b quant variants. comparing FP16 baseline, int8, int4 across two slices: short-chat (<=64 tokens) and longform-recall (>512 tokens). noticed an odd recall delta on longform.

dmitri: Results pasted below. quick notes first: int4 looks great on cost but shows quality drop on longform. int8 is a nice middle ground.


- cost per 1M tokens (approx): FP16 $12.0, int8 $7.9, int4 $4.4
- longform recall (relative to FP16): int8 -1.1% abs, int4 -4.8% abs
- short-chat quality: int8 ~0.0%, int4 -0.6%
- p50 latency (short-chat): FP16 78ms, int8 64ms, int4 72ms
- p95 latency (longform): FP16 420ms, int8 390ms, int4 410ms (int4 shows some tail due to rebatched kv cache hits)


eva: Can you paste the actual bench commands and the eval metric that measured "recall"?

dmitri: Sure. bench command we used: `./bench --model ceres-13b --quant={fp16,int8,int4} --slice={short,longform} --batch=auto --tokens=200k`

And eval-bot posted the automated slice scores after each run:
```
eval-bot: run_id=ceres-2026-03-20-01
metrics: {"longform_recall": {"fp16": 0.783, "int8": 0.772, "int4": 0.735}, "rouge_l": {"fp16": 0.412, "int8": 0.407, "int4": 0.398}}
```

kevin: So int4 is ~6% relative recall loss on longform vs fp16 (4.8% absolute). That's material for any product relying on long context. Do we have error cases or sample diffs?

rachel: Yep — diffs are concentrated on long, multi-turn reference retrieval tasks where the model drops a supporting fact in generated lists. Short chat replies are fine. Example diff: with int4 the model omits the second citation in ~3/50 long tests.

dmitri: Also observed a small increase in token emission variance on int4 which makes some downstream token-billing spike patterns a little noisier.

eva: OK. Given numbers, my suggestion for rollout: treat int4 as an efficiency tier only for short-chat and constrained prompt shapes. For any >512 token context, stick to int8 (or fp16 if latency/quality critical).

rachel: Proposed canary plan:
- Start with 5% global traffic to int4 but only for short-chat route (<=64).
- Keep longform pinned to int8 for now.
- Monitor these signals over 48h: short-chat p95 latency, short-chat correctness sample (automated quick eval), and longform recall regression (should be unchanged).
- Roll forward if short-chat QoQ delta <0.5% and latency/cost behave as expected. rollback immediately on any longform regression or customer complaint spike.

kevin: Mechanically, that's easy: create routing policy `route:ceres13b_quant_experiment_v1` with two rules. Also add a fallback: if eval-bot detects longform_recall drop >1% on moving window, switch all int4 traffic to int8.

dmitri: I can wire the fallback hook. simple pseudocode: `if moving_window_delta("longform_recall", "int4", "int8") < -0.01: set_route_weight(int4,0)`

eva: One more ask — can we add a small hybrid strategy later: for longform, allow int4 for prefix-only scoring (cheap prefilter), then rerank top-K with int8 to recover recall while retaining some cost win? worth testing in a second phase.

rachel: Agreed. Phase 2 = prefilter-int4 + rerank-int8 for long searches. Track unit-econ delta: cost per completed request, and end-to-end recall. Aim for >=25% cost reduction vs int8 while keeping recall within 1% abs.

kevin: Who owns the canary dashboard and alert? sugg: dmitri for data pipeline + infra-bot to post alerts. I can add the SLO/alert thresholds to the runbook.

dmitri: I'll add the dashboard: metrics = {short_chat_p95, short_chat_automated_precision, longform_recall_moving, cost_per_1k_tokens_by_quant}. Will post config in #eng-ml after setup.

rachel: OK — decision: no immediate int4 global rollout. Start the short-chat canary (5% -> 10% after 6h if stable). Longform remains int8. Phase 2 hybrid prefilter plan to follow once we have canary data. :thumbsup:

kevin: Sounds good. I'll update the canary playbook and link it in the experiment ticket.

eva: Thanks — nice quick sanity pass.

dmitri: posting raw diffs + sample cases to the ticket now: https://redwood-internal/issue/ML-1372

eval-bot: Canary monitor created: ceres13b_quant_experiment_v1_monitor (alerts: longform_recall_drop>1%, short_chat_p95>200ms)

rachel: Closing thread — followups in ticket ML-1372 and the dashboard.
